main_body: Flat snow ground patch (4x3 tiles) with a repeating pattern of grey-green drifts, white sparkle pixels and light-blue patches
top_band: none (ground terrain, no standing volume; the column scan shows repeating texture runs, not a top band over a front face)
evidence: This is a seamless ground surface, not a standing object, so the 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply. No receding side faces and no fake front elevation are drawn. A flat ground texture is the expected form for terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 7 distinct colours in total, against 80 for the grass reference. Its median of 7 colours per tile matches the paving reference but is far below grass at 26. Dark pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline reads as a dark material tone, and there are no 5x5 flat fills. The shading ramp is shallow: dark green-grey, mid grey-green, a lighter grey-green, light blue and white. The texture is a mechanical 16px repeat of the same blob and sparkle motif, with no per-clump variation, so it looks stamped rather than hand-shaded like the Beodeul grass. Next to the grass it would look thinner and more patterned, so it fails.
